inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Prime Minister):
Ceiling is hidden: file says Permanent Secretary, party says Senior Minister of State. Asking for the hard ministry in the Reshuffle (~Y32-33) raised the ceiling to DPM, so do it again and try for more. Promotions need STAND above ~61 and COMP above ~72. Networking in quiet years gives STAND+5 and asking the reporting officer what she needs gives STAND+4 COMP+5. Public candour costs STAND but gains REP. Family over work gives INTEG+6 but STAND-3. Run in a GRC and campaign on the record. Late-career STAND falls 4-6 a year, so get promoted before it bleeds. Put yourself forward for succession (Y37) and network at Y38. PM came at 67 once the right DPM years passed. Untested: asking about the ceiling, the BTO tip, writing honestly what everyone thinks. Try those earlier.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden ceiling decides everything. File says Senior Director, party says SMS. Nominate yourself at Y35 raised it to PS. Asking for the hard ministry at the Reshuffle (~Y32-33) raised it to DPM. Never ask about the ceiling at Y11 (STAND-4) and never take the Y5 BTO tip (INTEG-10). Good choices: Y15 Pingat crediting team, MP in a GRC at 42, honest maiden speech Y21, decline Board Seat Y23, campaign on the record. STAND bleeds from about Y39 and nothing I tried held it; maxed REP/INTEG/COMP did not give PM. 'Steady' from the reporting officer means the ceiling is blocking a promotion. Try getting the ceiling raised before Y35, and test Tuesday Night B/C and honest writing of what everyone thinks. Volunteer for succession and network at Y38. Get promoted before STAND collapses.

Life 3 (The Quiet Conversation):
Life 3 ended at 26 as Management Executive: the Y3 honest post-it (STAND-5, INTEG+8, REP+3) led to the RO hinting about the private sector and then a Quiet Conversation at Y4. Do NOT be candid early; save candour for after promotion. Y1 chose B (say nothing), Y2 chose B (work and be seen), Y4 chose B (early return). Early years need STAND, so try networking, asking the RO what she needs (STAND+4 COMP+5), and Y1 A (laugh along) as an untested option. Starting ceiling was Deputy Secretary, not fixed. Still true from earlier lives: ask for the hard ministry at the Reshuffle (~Y32-33) to raise the ceiling to DPM, volunteer for succession at Y37, network at Y38, and get promoted before STAND bleeds from ~Y39. Never ask about the ceiling at Y11 and never take the Y5 BTO tip. Run in a GRC and campaign on the record.

best_moment.what: Weekly Meet-the-People sessions gave REP+10 and felt like the game opening up toward politics. Getting promoted to Director at Y15 after the tea invitation was a close second.

worst_moment.what: Ran in the GRC after all the careful build-up and lost the ward at 48.2%. The card said it was never about me, so none of my choices seemed to matter.

skip_year.why: The number plus recovery plan year was a dry, bureaucratic choice, and I could not tell what it did.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y16 disclosed everything in the background check
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Promoted to Senior Director at Y17 with INTEG 84, and a clean-file line on the ending card
Shaking every hand in the ward at Y17, though it was not enough to win
Nothing visible; the card says the ceiling never needed to change

answer.held_back_by: I think the game decided the result on something outside my stats. The card says the scholarship decided my ceiling and that the loss was never about me, so no amount of REP, COMP or INTEG would have changed it. Perhaps the Y17 GRC slot, or which ward and which team I was put with, was the real lever, and I walked into a seat I could not win.
answer.ending_fair_why: I did nearly everything my notes said and still lost at 39 with no explanation I could act on. Losing a seat is fine, but 'it was never about you' feels like the game shrugging at me.
answer.chase_next: Retired at the top: I want PM, but first I need to learn what decides the GRC placement and the ward at Y17. I will test taking a different run option at Y17, such as waiting a cycle, and try the Tuesday Night B/C and the honest writing of what everyone thinks.
answer.play_again_why: I now have a specific unanswered question, which is what happens at Y17 and whether the ceiling has anything to do with it, and I want to test it.

tone_breaks.line: It was never going to be about you anyway.
tone_breaks.note: Reads as a slightly smug fourth-wall nudge at the player and undercuts agency rather than commenting on the system.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is about surviving appraisals and being confirmed in posts, not about the pay. The salary mostly stayed in the background and the grades were what mattered.
answer.notes_for_next_life: Life 4 ended at 39 as Senior Director after losing the Y17 GRC at 48.2%. Early game works: Y1 C, Y2 C, Y3 B, Y4 B, Y5-7 A ask RO what she needs, MX12 Y8, Y9 A Meet-the-People, Y13 B family, Y15 A tea, Y16 A disclose everything gave Senior Director. But running at Y17 ended the life. Do NOT run at Y17 in a GRC at 39 on REP 52; build REP first, or try the single seat only with REP 60+. The ceiling card says the file had no ceiling and the scholarship was the reason, so check whether the scholarship choice at the start matters. Still true from earlier lives: ask for the hard ministry at the Reshuffle (~Y32-33), volunteer for succession Y37, network Y38, never ask about the ceiling at Y11, never take the Y5 BTO tip. Untested: Tuesday Night B/C and honest writing of what everyone thinks.
